title: Growing Overnight Bacterial Culture in 96-Well Plates
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfs9jnh6

steps.title: Prepare LB broth
steps.instruction: Obtain LB broth from the media kitchen and make it by mixing 4 g NaCl, 4 g tryptone, and 2 g yeast extract, then add de‑ionized water to a final volume of 400 mL.

steps.title: Sterilize work area
steps.instruction: Wipe the bench with 70 % ethanol, create a relatively sterile environment using a gas‑powered burner, and work under a hood if many plates are used (book the hood in advance).

steps.title: Label plates and lids
steps.instruction: Label each inoculation plate and its lid with the corresponding frozen library plate ID.

steps.title: Add LB to wells
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette and a sterile reservoir, dispense 200 µL of liquid LB into each well of a Nunc MicroWell plate (Nunclon Delta Surface‑C, ThermoFisher Scientific, catalogue 143761, well capacity 300 µL).

steps.title: Retrieve frozen library plates
steps.instruction: Remove the frozen library plates from the –80 °C freezer immediately before inoculation; optionally keep them on dry ice and, just before use, place each plate on the bench for 2 min to thaw slightly.

steps.title: Position plates and mark A1
steps.instruction: Arrange plates so that well A1 is at the top‑left corner; optionally place stickers on the replicator to mark wells A1 and H12 to avoid confusion.

steps.title: Prepare replicator with tape
steps.instruction: Wrap laboratory/masking tape around the index and middle fingers, adhesive side outward, and use the tape’s stickiness to grip the sterile replicator by gently pressing on its surface.

steps.title: Inoculate wells with replicator
steps.instruction: Insert the sterile replicator into each frozen library well (touch or puncture the frozen surface to pick up cells), then dip it into the corresponding inoculation plate wells, swirling slightly to mix bacteria with the LB.

steps.title: Sterilize replicator after use
steps.instruction: Place the used replicator into an autoclavable box for sterilization; use one replicator per inoculation plate to prevent cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Seal inoculation plates
steps.instruction: Cover each inoculation plate with plastic lids and/or breathable seals (Axygen Rayon breathable film, 50 µm, catalogue AXY2008).

steps.title: Incubate plates
steps.instruction: If plates are not to be shaken, place them in an airtight box and incubate; otherwise incubate with shaking (150–180 rpm) ensuring the liquid volume does not exceed two‑thirds of well capacity (≤200 µL for 300 µL wells). Incubate at the required growth temperature overnight (12–18 h); if shaking at any temperature other than 37 °C, book the shaking incubator in advance.

steps.title: Assess bacterial growth
steps.instruction: After incubation, examine each well for a cloudy haze, indicating bacterial growth.
